title: A bug filed at the end of a task has been reproduced, not just read
goal: A task that finished last night filed a top priority bug saying the loop had stopped rebuilding the app you playtest with, so nobody was seeing their work. It was not true: the check that found it ran the wrong shell against the script, and the rebuild had in fact run and succeeded minutes earlier. A follow-up filed from reading rather than running costs a whole task cycle at the top of the queue, so the instructions a task runner works from should require the same standard for a bug it files as for the work it does.
notes: Design review 2026-09-06. Evidence: the-app-you-playtest-with-is-rebuilt-after-every, created 12:10 UTC, dropped in the same triage pass. Its notes said queue/bin/refresh-dev-app.sh was a bash syntax error; the file is #!/bin/zsh and zsh -n is clean, queue/loop.log holds 180 successful refreshes with the last at 05:10:36 the same morning, and go-loop.sh:125 already prints a line when a refresh fails, which the task also said was missing. queue/bin/runner-prompt.md has no rule about reproducing a bug before filing it (grep for reproduce finds nothing).
acceptance: The runner instructions say a follow-up that claims something is broken must carry the command that shows it broken, and its output
They say to run a script the way the machine runs it rather than reading it or checking it with another shell
They say what to do when it cannot be reproduced: file it as something to look into rather than as a bug, at normal priority
The daily triage pass is told to spot-check the evidence on any new top priority bug before it is allowed to run first
